facts.raw_span: discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla
severe pruritus at these sites that would wake him up at night
denied any recent trauma or history of similar lesions
denied associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms (eg, fever, chills)
3 well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion that are limited to his right axilla
No other lesions were noted on his skin or mucous membranes
A Wood lamp examination was negative
lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction
treatment with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, and discontinuation of underarm deodorant yielded no improvement

concepts.why: The patient presents with discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla, severe pruritus, and no improvement with treatment, which are consistent with contact dermatitis.
The patient's lesions are well-circumscribed, violaceous, and annular, and he has severe pruritus, which are characteristic of atopic dermatitis.
The patient's biopsy findings show lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction, which is consistent with lichen planus.
The patient's lesions are discrete, dark red, and circular, and he has severe pruritus, which are characteristic of dyshidrotic eczema.

rationales.F05: The description of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches is highly suggestive of lichen planus.
